summary: Deep dive focused on instrumenting Redwood runtime with OpenTelemetry for token-level metrics and traces. Discussed span design (preprocess -> routing -> queue -> kernel -> postprocess), tradeoffs of metrics vs traces for high-cardinality attributes, KV cache hit instrumentation, sample rates, and VPC deployment considerations for OTLP exporters. Agreed next steps: share collector config, dashboards, and run a 1-hour benchmark.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-17
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~55m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Luis Ortega (Redwood SE), Priya Raman (Head of ML Infra - Acero Labs), Ethan Wu (SRE - Acero), Nora Klein (Security - Acero)

Summary (auto): Deep technical walkthrough of OpenTelemetry integration, token-level metrics, dashboards, and VPC/collector considerations.

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We'll do a deep dive on observability and tracing with OpenTelemetry, specifically how to get token-level metrics out of the Redwood runtime. Luis will drive the tech details.
[00:18] Luis Ortega: Hey all. Quick agenda: how we instrument inference flow, what to surface as metrics vs traces, collector topology (in-cluster vs external), perf overhead, and dashboard/alert examples.
[00:36] Priya Raman: Sounds good. Our goals are twofold: 1) be able to alert on perf regressions at token granularity, and 2) correlate model quality regressions to perf/cost. We run on-prem for some sensitive workloads so VPC/OTLP egress is a thing.
[00:55] Ethan Wu: +1, also curious about cardinality - we have thousands of tenants. High-card tags will explode our metrics storage.
[01:10] Luis Ortega: Totally. We recommend low-cardinality labels on Prometheus metrics (model_family, hardware_type, region) and push high-cardinality details into traces or logs (request_id, user_id, prompt_hash).
[01:32] Nora Klein: Security question up front: does Redwood's collector require outbound internet? For Private/VPC we can't have external egress for telemetry.
[01:45] Maya Chen: Good call. We support a local OTLP collector inside the VPC/on-prem cluster. You can run the collector as sidecar or daemonset and then export to your internal backend (Jaeger/Honeycomb/Splunk) or to a private Grafana Cloud endpoint.
[02:03] Priya Raman: Ok. Can you walk through the spans you emit for a single request? We want to map downstream traces to our SLOs.
[02:18] Luis Ortega: Sure. Typical span tree we instrument: client request -> preprocess (tokenization, prompt transform) -> routing/queue (which includes batching metadata) -> runtime enqueue/dequeue -> kernel execution (per-chunk spans, includes quantization exec path) -> kv_cache_lookup span (we set attribute kv_cache_hit=true/false) -> postprocess (detokenize, filter).
[02:44] Luis Ortega: We also emit per-token events inside the kernel execution span with timestamps for token_gen_start/token_gen_end if you want exact per-token latency; those are expensive if you sample 100% so we recommend sampling or summarizing into histograms.
[03:04] Ethan Wu: So token events are events not metrics? How do we get token-per-second as a metric?
[03:15] Luis Ortega: We aggregate token rates into Prometheus counters (tokens_generated_total) and expose derived rates (tokens/sec) with low-cardinality labels. For per-token latency distributions we push histograms (p50, p95, p99) for per-request token latency, but not per-token label for every tenant.
[03:34] Priya Raman: What about KV cache hits - we want to know the hit ratio by model/tenant.
[03:42] Luis Ortega: For KV cache, we emit metrics kv_cache_hits_total and kv_cache_misses_total with labels model_variant and tenant_id* (tenant_id is high-cardinality; we recommend using tenant tier or hashed bucket in metrics, and full tenant_id in traces).
[04:01] Ethan Wu: Hashing buckets is OK. How about quantization paths - does the runtime annotate whether a request used q4/q8 or fp16?
[04:11] Luis Ortega: Yes, we add attribute model_quantization with values like q4f16, q8, fp16 on the kernel span and also as a low-cardinality field on aggregated metrics (we keep quantization as a small set).
[04:26] Priya Raman: Overhead concerns - you mentioned per-token events are expensive. What's realistic overhead on p99 latency if we enable full spans + events at 10% sampling?
[04:39] Luis Ortega: In our benchmarks, 10% sampling with per-token events added about 2-5% CPU overhead on the CPU side and ~5-10% tail latency increase for small models in tight lat SLOs. For large models the overhead is lower relatively, but the network/collector bandwidth matters.
[04:59] Maya Chen: For hard SLOs we'd do sampling and push detailed traces only for anomalous requests — for example, dynamically increase sampling when p95 token latency crosses threshold.
[05:14] Priya Raman: That dynamic sampling sounds great. Is that supported out-of-the-box?
[05:20] Luis Ortega: We can tie runtime alerts to the collector config; we provide example policies in the collector config we will share.
[05:28] Ethan Wu: How do we correlate SLO violations across routing and hardware? We have multiple GPU pools (A100 and H100) and sometimes workloads jump between them.
[05:40] Luis Ortega: Each span contains hardware_type, node_id, and model_variant. Traces let you see the end-to-end path and where time was spent. For metrics you can slice by hardware_type and node_pool label, but be cautious with too many node-specific labels.
[05:58] Priya Raman: Can you show an example Grafana dashboard layout?
[06:04] Luis Ortega: Sure, I have a sample we use: top row SLOs (tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99 token latency), second row per-model throughput and cost per 1000 tokens, third row KV cache hit ratio and batching efficiency (avg batch size, batch wait time), bottom row tracer sampling rate and dropped spans. We'll share JSON.
[06:26] Priya Raman: Perfect. Please include an example alert rule for batch wait time.
[06:31] Luis Ortega: Example: alert if avg_batch_wait_time_ms_p95 > 50ms for 5m AND tokens/sec < expected baseline. This indicates bad batching policy.
[06:44] Nora Klein: Security again: traces contain prompt hashes and partial prompts at times. Are those redacted? How do you recommend handling PII?
[06:56] Luis Ortega: By default we don't include raw prompt content in traces. We emit prompt_hash and prompt_length. If customers want raw content, they opt-in and must configure encryption/retention. For VPC/private installs the traces never leave customer infra unless you opt in.
[07:13] Priya Raman: Where do you put the OTLP collector in a private deployment? Sidecar or daemonset? Pros/cons?
[07:21] Luis Ortega: Daemonset is preferred for lower CPU footprint per pod and simpler topology; sidecar provides per-pod isolation but more overhead. For high-throughput inference nodes, use a local daemonset collector with batching and compression to internal observability backend.
[07:38] Ethan Wu: Network bandwidth - will exporting traces for 10% sample blow our private network?
[07:45] Luis Ortega: It can. We recommend local buffering and batching in the collector, use compression (OTLP/gRPC gzip), and tune sample rates. Also consider exporting only aggregated metrics to Prometheus remote_write and sending traces to a different path.
[08:05] Priya Raman: Let's talk about token-level dashboards for cost: we want cost per 1k tokens per model/quantization.
[08:14] Luis Ortega: We expose estimate_cost_per_1000_tokens metric computed from hardware cost coefficients and model throughput. We tag by model_family and quantization. The dashboard includes cost vs quality tradeoff curves.
[08:28] Priya Raman: Nice. How do we instrument kernel quantization differences? For example if a model falls back to fp16 because q4 path not available, we need to see that.
[08:39] Luis Ortega: Kernel span includes fallback_reason and exec_kernel_version. Fallbacks show up in traces and we emit a metric kernel_fallback_total with label fallback_reason.
[08:51] Ethan Wu: Any gotchas around batching? We currently observed that batching sometimes increases tail latency even though throughput improves.
[08:59] Luis Ortega: Right - batch wait time vs compute time tradeoff. We emit avg_batch_size and batch_wait_time_ms metrics. You can set autoscaling/batching policies per route. For latency-sensitive routes we recommend max_batch_size=1 or use low-latency batching windows.
[09:19] Priya Raman: Can we get token-level traces for only routes tagged 'interactive' while leaving background jobs low-sampled?
[09:28] Luis Ortega: Yep - route-level sampling rules are standard. We recommend route labels and sampler rules in the collector.
[09:36] Priya Raman: How do you handle high-cardinality attributes like prompt templates?
[09:42] Luis Ortega: Avoid adding prompt templates as metric labels. Hash them and put hash in metrics; full template goes into trace payloads if necessary, or to a separate logging store with retention policies.
[09:54] Maya Chen: Quick pause - Nora, any red flags from security?
[09:58] Nora Klein: Mostly two items: retention of traces, and where encryption keys live when exporting. We need KMS integration for private installs.
[10:07] Maya Chen: We support KMS/HSM integrations and can configure the collector to use your key management for any persisted telemetry. We'll include details in the security pack.
[10:18] Ethan Wu: Can we see an OTLP config now?
[10:21] Luis Ortega: I'll paste a snippet after the call; but high level: collector as daemonset, receivers: otlp (gRPC), processors: batch/attributes/prefix, exporters: prometheusremote or otlp to your internal tracing system. We have example configs for Grafana Loki, Jaeger, Honeycomb.
[10:42] Priya Raman: Do you have examples of trace-based alerts?
[10:45] Luis Ortega: Yes - e.g., alert when traces with kv_cache_hit=false and kernel_fallback_total > threshold co-occur with p95 token latency spike. That often indicates cache eviction or model rollback.
[10:58] Priya Raman: About deployment topology - in our on-prem cluster some nodes are air-gapped. How do we collect from those?
[11:06] Luis Ortega: For air-gapped, run a local observability backend (e.g., Grafana + Prometheus + Jaeger) inside the air-gapped network. Collector exports stay internal. We can help with an on-prem package.
[11:19] Maya Chen: We have an on-prem Private product specifically for that use-case; it bundles agent/collector best practices.
[11:27] Ethan Wu: Any concerns about metrics cardinality from dynamic model_version tags?
[11:33] Luis Ortega: Keep model_version coarse-grained (major version) as a label; full git SHA or build id should go to traces. We also recommend tag recycling and retention policies in Prometheus.
[11:48] Priya Raman: Let's talk about ingestion cost - e.g., if we send all metrics to Grafana Cloud, cost explodes. Do you have guidelines?
[11:58] Luis Ortega: Yes - aggregate aggressively at the collector, drop high-card streams, and use remote_write for aggregated metrics. Also use sampling and dynamic sampling to control trace volume.
[12:12] Priya Raman: Any pre-built dashboards you can share for our SRE team?
[12:16] Luis Ortega: Yes, will include sample Grafana JSONs with panels for SLOs, throughput, KV cache, batching and quantization.
[12:25] Nora Klein: For auditing, do you emit immutable logs for request metadata?
[12:31] Luis Ortega: We can stream audit logs to your SIEM. Audit logs include request_id, model_variant, tenant_id (or hashed) and decision events (model_rollout, fallback).
[12:45] Priya Raman: How do you surface per-tenant cost back to billing?
[12:50] Luis Ortega: We attach cost allocation labels to aggregated metrics and export to our billing connector. For private installs we provide a connector that maps tokens_generated_total per tenant to your billing system.
[13:05] Maya Chen: Quick question on integration timeline - if Acero wants a Dedicated pilot with full telemetry, what's the typical setup time?
[13:13] Luis Ortega: For Dedicated in cloud ~2-3 weeks including collector config and dashboards; for on-prem Private with air-gapped clusters it's 4-6 weeks.
[13:23] Priya Raman: Budget/timeline align — we were hoping to run a pilot in July.
[13:28] Maya Chen: That fits. We'll follow up with a pilot plan.
[13:32] Ethan Wu: One more deep tech question: do you annotate KV cache hits at the per-token level?
[13:38] Luis Ortega: We annotate kv_cache_hit at the span level and emit kv_cache_hit_count as a metric. Per-token boolean can be emitted as events but it's high-volume; we usually recommend a sampled view.
[13:54] Priya Raman: For SLOs we need continuous 1-minute granularity p95 token latency across routes. Is Prometheus good enough for that?
[14:05] Luis Ortega: Yes, with proper retention and aggregation. Use recording rules to precompute p95 over 1m windows. For long tail/forensic, use traces.
[14:18] Priya Raman: Regarding function/tool calling and streaming — do you instrument stream chunks?
[14:25] Luis Ortega: We emit stream_chunk events with sequence numbers and track chunk latency. For streaming endpoints we emit metrics for chunk throughput and chunk_error_rate.
[14:38] Ethan Wu: Any sample size guidance for traces when debugging performance issues?
[14:43] Luis Ortega: Start with 1-5% sampling globally and raise to 50-100% for the route/time window where anomaly detected. Also keep a rolling buffer of full traces for e.g., 24-72 hours.
[14:58] Priya Raman: Let's get into an example: we saw a p99 spike yesterday. How would we triage with your telemetry?
[15:06] Luis Ortega: First check metrics: p99 token latency by model_variant and hardware_type, kv_cache_hit_ratio, avg_batch_size, batch_wait_time. If those point to cache misses or smaller batch sizes, look at traces for that time window to find if fallback_reason or long kernel_exec spans occurred.
[15:26] Priya Raman: Ok. Can you walk through a real trace snippet?
[15:30] Luis Ortega: Sure, (reads) root span request_id=abc123 -> preprocessing 3ms -> routing 2ms -> queue wait 48ms (batch_size=16) -> kernel_exec 120ms (quantization=q4f16, node_id=gpu-23) -> kv_lookup hit=false -> postprocess 4ms. You can see most time in kernel and queue.
[15:56] Ethan Wu: That queue wait stands out. Could be due to autoscaler oscillation.
[16:02] Luis Ortega: Right. We also surface pod scale events in the dashboard.
[16:10] Priya Raman: For the kernel_exec span, is the time broken down per-layer or only aggregate?
[16:17] Luis Ortega: We offer optional layer-level timing for debugging (per-layer spans) but it's very high volume and usually sampled for heavy models.
[16:29] Nora Klein: If we opt-in to layer-level spans, can we encrypt those traces at rest?
[16:34] Luis Ortega: Yes, encryption at rest with customer KMS is supported. We'll document config.
[16:43] Priya Raman: Any gotchas with Prometheus histogram buckets for latency?
[16:47] Luis Ortega: Use exponential buckets tuned to your latency SLOs; avoid too many buckets. Also precompute percentiles with recording rules to avoid expensive queries.
[16:59] Ethan Wu: Regarding exporters, do you support OTLP over HTTP or only gRPC?
[17:04] Luis Ortega: Both; gRPC is more efficient but HTTP works if you have proxy constraints.
[17:11] Priya Raman: For routing policies, can telemetry tag requests that were routed to a fallback model?
[17:17] Luis Ortega: Yes we tag span attribute routed_model_variant and fallback_flag=true if a fallback occurred. That ties directly into rollback detection.
[17:28] Priya Raman: How do you avoid blowing up metrics from per-tenant labels across hundreds of models?
[17:33] Luis Ortega: Use aggregation at the collector, rollup to tenant_tier or tenant_bucket labels, and store full cardinality in traces only. Also apply per-tenant retention policies.
[17:49] Maya Chen: Quick break - Luis will demo a dashboard in the follow-up email.
[17:55] (short pause)
[18:03] Luis Ortega: A couple more notes: we expose token generation time as a cumulative histogram so you can compute p50/p95/p99. We also expose token_wait_time which isolates scheduling delays (batch wait).
[18:21] Priya Raman: How do you instrument client-side vs server-side times for RT comparisons?
[18:26] Luis Ortega: We accept client timestamp in trace attributes and compute time skew; also we emit client_to_server_latency metric if you propagate request_start. Helps correlate network vs server time.
[18:39] Ethan Wu: Anything special for multi-tenant isolation telemetry?
[18:44] Luis Ortega: We recommend tenant-scoped collectors or tenant_id label hashing plus strict RBAC in the observability backends. For private installs you can enforce separation at the storage layer.
[18:58] Priya Raman: Ok, let's capture concrete next steps.
[19:03] Maya Chen: We'll summarize now. Luis, action items?
[19:07] Luis Ortega: I'll share: 1) example OTLP collector config (daemonset) 2) sample Grafana dashboards (SLOs, KV cache, batching) 3) example recording rules and alerting rules.
[19:20] Maya Chen: I'll send the security whitepaper and SOC2 artifacts, plus the dedicated pilot pricing.
[19:27] Priya Raman: We'll schedule a 1-hour benchmark the week of 6/22 and share results.
[19:33] Ethan Wu: We'll also provide list of critical routes to monitor.
[19:37] Maya Chen: Great. Anything else?
[19:40] Nora Klein: Please ensure the collector config includes attribute filtering so we don't accidentally log PII.
[19:46] Luis Ortega: We'll add attribute redaction examples.
[19:50] Maya Chen: Perfect. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the artifacts and a calendar invite for the benchmark.
[19:58] (wrap up)
